body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18), who has a Tormach 770MX: "you can use a 3d mill like a lathe ... You end up using multiple WCS for each tool and put part in spindle". Wording: this is **turning on a mill (part in spindle)**, not live tooling on a lathe (CamCraft's existing "Mill-turn" machine).

## The setup

- The workpiece is held in a collet in the mill spindle and turns (M3/M4 at lathe speeds).
- Lathe tools (turning, facing, grooving, threading, parting) are clamped on the table in a gang row.
- There is no tool change: each tool is selected by switching to its own work offset (G54...G59, G59.1-3, G54.1 Pn) whose origin is that tool's tip relative to the spindle centre line.
- One length offset describes the part in the spindle: collet nose to the end of the stock stick-out (`G43 H<n>` once; the user keeps T255 for it).
- Lathe Z (along the part) is the mill Z; lathe X (diameter) is a table axis toward the spindle centre line.

## What CamCraft does today (QA run p09, main `83867fd7`)

- No way to declare "part in spindle, tools on the table".
- A lathe operation set accepted on a 3-axis mill machine posts lathe code labelled "Tormach 770MX" with no warning (high; filed separately).

## Open questions

1. Machine description: a part-in-spindle mode, tool stations on the table (position, side of the spindle, WCS), the collet nose and the stock stick-out.
2. Operations: reuse the turning operations; what changes in the X sign and spindle direction per side; constant surface speed vs fixed RPM on a mill spindle; feed per rev.
3. Post: a WCS switch per tool, no M6, safe retracts between stations, the one `G43 H` for the stock.
4. Safety checks: tool blocks vs the collet and the part, max spindle RPM with a part in it, chip direction.
5. Sources: Tormach's public RapidTurn documentation (operator manual UM10393, D32901, TD10561); the user's own 770MX tests.

Plan (user): several CamCraft simulations first, then PathPilot Hub, then air cuts, then real cuts - slowly.
